# Command reference

[README](../README.md) · [Getting started](GETTING_STARTED.md) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md)

`wgfeel` runs one instance with independent `main`/`child` control and `entry`/`relay`/`off` traffic capabilities.
Installations use one executable and one service.

`[VALUE]` is optional; uppercase values are placeholders. Quote names containing
spaces. Public endpoints below use documentation-only addresses: replace them
with your own. Interactive selection uses numbers; explicit arguments use IDs.

## Contents

- [Connection options](#connection-options)
- [wgfeel](#wgfeel)

## Connection options

Administrative commands connect to the installed main Unix socket automatically. A downloaded binary defaults to /opt/wgfeel; an installed binary uses its own installation base. Alternatively, pass either --profile or both --socket and --credential-file. Connection options may appear anywhere after user, device, egress, node or config. File ownership and permission checks still apply.

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--profile PATH` | Use a private administrator profile for remote access over WireGuard. Cannot be combined with --socket or --credential-file. |
| `--socket PATH` | Use a local main Unix socket; requires --credential-file. |
| `--credential-file PATH` | Read the administrator credential from an owned regular file with mode 0600; requires --socket. |

<a id="wgfeel-install"></a>

### wgfeel install

```text
wgfeel install [--control main|child] [OPTIONS]
```

Install the wgfeel executable, wgfeel.service, manual page, shell completions and protected state under instance/. Run without arguments for interactive menus. On main, choose the traffic mode, HTTP API port and WireGuard UDP port. A child stays stopped until wgfeel join. Existing state is preserved; use wgfeel update to upgrade.

| Argument / option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--control main\|child` | Control capability; required for noninteractive installation. |
| `--traffic entry\|relay\|off` | Main's user-traffic capability; default entry. Child traffic policy is assigned by main. |
| `--port PORT` | WireGuard UDP port on main, also assigned to children at join. Default 51820. |
| `--endpoint ADDRESS` | Advertised address. Main takes IP:port or [IPv6]:port. Child takes a bare IPv4 or IPv6 address. Repeat in preference order. |
| `--listen-ip IP` | UDP bind IP. Defaults to the wildcard address matching the endpoint family. |
| `--id ID` | Unique persistent node name. Defaults to main or the child’s short hostname. If the hostname is unavailable or invalid, a child gets a generated ID. |
| `--api-port PORT` | External REST HTTP/TCP port on main; default 9280. Change it later with wgfeel api port PORT. |
| `--api-listen-ip IP` | HTTP bind IP on main; default 127.0.0.1. |
| `--install-dir PATH` | Installation base. Defaults to the running installed binary's base, or /opt/wgfeel for a downloaded binary. |
| `--root ABS` | Stage filesystem paths below this absolute root. Requires --no-start or --dry-run; defaults to /. |
| `--dry-run` | Preview the operation without writing files or controlling services. |
| `--no-start` | Keep the service stopped after installation and after child enrollment. |

Example:

```sh
wgfeel install --control main --traffic entry \
  --endpoint 192.0.2.1:51820 --api-port 9280
wgfeel install --control child --endpoint 192.0.2.2
```

<a id="wgfeel-update"></a>

### wgfeel update

```text
wgfeel update [OPTIONS]
```

Replace the installed executable and refresh its manual and shell completions from the newly copied binary. Preserve configuration, keys and service settings; retain the previous binary and restart the previously active service. No downloads are performed.

| Argument / option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--install-dir PATH` | Installation base. Defaults to the running installed binary's base, or /opt/wgfeel for a downloaded binary. |
| `--root ABS` | Stage filesystem paths below this absolute root. Requires --no-start or --dry-run; defaults to /. |
| `--dry-run` | Preview the operation without writing files or controlling services. |
| `--no-start` | Skip service control; the instance must be stopped. |

Example:

```sh
./wgfeel.new update --dry-run
./wgfeel.new update
```

<a id="wgfeel-uninstall"></a>

### wgfeel uninstall

```text
wgfeel uninstall [OPTIONS]
```

Remove the receipt-owned service, executable and command resources. Keep state and keys unless purge is explicitly confirmed. Preview first with --dry-run.

| Argument / option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--install-dir PATH` | Installation base. Defaults to the running installed binary's base, or /opt/wgfeel for a downloaded binary. |
| `--dry-run` | Preview the operation without writing files or controlling services. |
| `--purge` | Also delete recorded configuration and state; requires confirmation. |
| `--confirm wgfeel` | Noninteractive confirmation for --purge. |

Example:

```sh
wgfeel uninstall --dry-run
wgfeel uninstall
wgfeel uninstall --purge --confirm wgfeel
```

<a id="wgfeel-api-port"></a>

### wgfeel api port

```text
wgfeel api port [PORT] [OPTIONS]
```

Show or change the external REST HTTP listener port on this main. The running service opens the new listener before saving the setting and closing the old one. A stopped service saves the setting for its next start. Does not change WireGuard, device profiles or keys. Only the local owner can perform this operation.

| Argument / option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--state-dir PATH` | Local state directory. Use the installed instance's state directory or an explicitly provisioned absolute path. |
| `--install-dir PATH` | Installation base. Defaults to the running installed binary's base, or /opt/wgfeel for a downloaded binary. |
| `PORT` | Optional TCP port, 1..65535. Omit to show the current HTTP address. |

Example:

```sh
wgfeel api port
wgfeel api port 8081
```

### wgfeel state-check

```text

```

| Argument / option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--state-dir PATH` | Local state directory. Use the installed instance's state directory or an explicitly provisioned absolute path. |

Example:


<a id="wgfeel-completions"></a>

### wgfeel completions

```text
wgfeel completions SHELL
```

Print shell integration for Bash or Zsh. Source it in the matching shell after enabling its standard completion system. Static commands require no connection. User, device, egress and node IDs are queried using the current administrator connection and permissions; unavailable data produces no dynamic suggestions.

| Argument / option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `SHELL` | bash or zsh. |

Example:

```sh
source <(wgfeel completions bash)
source <(wgfeel completions zsh)
```

<a id="wgfeel-init"></a>

### wgfeel init

```text
wgfeel init --control main|child [OPTIONS]
```

Initialize protected state for the selected control capability. Main owns authoritative configuration and defaults to entry traffic. Child starts unbound. Run the wgfeel join command issued by main to receive its configuration. Existing state is never overwritten.

| Argument / option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--control main\|child` | Required control capability. Only main can write authoritative configuration. |
| `--state-dir PATH` | Required absolute local state directory. |
| `--id ID` | Node identity; required for child initialization. |
| `--traffic entry\|relay\|off` | Main traffic capability. Default: entry. Child policy is assigned by main. |
| `--profile PATH` | Required private administrator profile destination for main. |
| `--listen IP:PORT` | Required main WireGuard UDP bind address. An advertised --endpoint is also required, including for a concrete bind address. |
| `--endpoint IP:PORT` | Required advertised main unicast IP and UDP port. IPv6 uses [address]:port. Child enrollment discovers its endpoints through join. |
| `--api-port PORT` | Enable the independent external HTTP API on main. Omitted means disabled for this low-level command. |
| `--api-listen-ip IP` | HTTP bind address on main; default 127.0.0.1. Requires --api-port. |

Example:

```sh
wgfeel init --control main --traffic entry \
  --state-dir /srv/wgfeel/state --profile /srv/wgfeel/admin.json \
  --listen 0.0.0.0:51820 --endpoint 192.0.2.1:51820 --api-port 9280
wgfeel init --control child --state-dir /srv/wgfeel/state --id child1
```

<a id="wgfeel-serve"></a>

### wgfeel serve

```text
wgfeel serve --control main|child --state-dir PATH [OPTIONS]
```

Run main or child in the foreground. Main uses its stored WireGuard and optional HTTP listeners. Installed children use --listen-ip and read the assigned port from their saved configuration. For a manually started child, pass --listen.

| Argument / option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--control main\|child` | Required control capability; it must match the initialized state. |
| `--state-dir PATH` | Local state directory. Use the installed instance's state directory or an explicitly provisioned absolute path. |
| `--listen IP:PORT` | Explicit WireGuard bind address for a manually started child. |
| `--listen-ip IP` | Bind an enrolled child at its assigned port. |

Example:

```sh
wgfeel serve --control main --state-dir /srv/wgfeel/state
wgfeel serve --control child --state-dir /srv/wgfeel/state \
  --listen 0.0.0.0:51820
```

<a id="wgfeel-join"></a>

### wgfeel join

```text
wgfeel join INVITATION|--invitation-stdin [OPTIONS]
```

Enroll the local child using a one-time invitation over service WireGuard on the shared UDP port. The installed child uses the UDP port from the invitation. Join enables and starts its service after saving configuration, unless installed with --no-start. Print main's UDP addresses immediately and progress every five seconds. Wait up to 75 seconds for durable configuration; a failed join preserves the previous binding unless replacement was committed.

| Argument / option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `INVITATION` | One-time URI from wgfeel node add. Prefer --invitation-stdin to keep the URI out of command arguments. |
| `--invitation-stdin` | Read a single invitation line from standard input. |
| `--install-dir PATH` | Installation base. Defaults to the running installed binary's base, or /opt/wgfeel for a downloaded binary. |
| `--state-dir PATH` | Local state directory. Use the installed instance's state directory or an explicitly provisioned absolute path. |
| `--endpoint IP:PORT` | Advertised child endpoint. Repeat for IPv4 and IPv6; normally discovered automatically. |

Example:

```sh
wgfeel join --invitation-stdin
```

<a id="wgfeel-user"></a>

### wgfeel user

```text
wgfeel user
```

Open the interactive administration menus. Select users and devices by number; names are separate from generated IDs. The menus also provide suspension and resumption of a user's isolated network.

Accepts the [connection options](#connection-options).

Example:

```sh

```

### wgfeel user list




<a id="wgfeel-user-add"></a>

### wgfeel user add

```text
wgfeel user add [NAME]
```

Create a user and its isolated network, ask for the first device name, then open the user's menu. IDs, addresses and keys are generated automatically. Names must be nonempty, at most 128 bytes, with no control characters or surrounding whitespace.

Accepts the [connection options](#connection-options).

| Argument / option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `NAME` | Friendly user name; quote names containing spaces. |

Example:

```sh
wgfeel user add Alice
```


<a id="wgfeel-node-add"></a>

### wgfeel node add

```text
wgfeel node add [OPTIONS]
```

Create a one-time invitation and print main's endpoints, the child UDP port and the wgfeel join command. Main fixes the traffic mode in the invitation; the child cannot override it. Re-enrolling an existing child requires its current mode. Treat the invitation as a credential.

Accepts the [connection options](#connection-options).

| Argument / option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--traffic entry\|relay\|off` | Child traffic capability. Default: entry. Relay carries ciphertext without tenant keys; off carries control traffic only. |
| `--revision NUMBER` | Require this positive configuration revision when issuing the invitation. Otherwise read the current revision first. An invitation does not reserve a revision for later enrollment. |

Example:

```sh
wgfeel node add
wgfeel node add --traffic relay
```

<a id="wgfeel-node-delete"></a>

### wgfeel node delete

```text
wgfeel node delete ID [--revision NUMBER]
```

Display the node and ask for confirmation before removing it from the configuration. Confirmation defaults to no.

Accepts the [connection options](#connection-options).

| Argument / option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `ID` | Required registered node ID. |
| `--revision NUMBER` | Expected positive configuration revision; otherwise use the current revision. |

<a id="wgfeel-token-rotate"></a>

### wgfeel token rotate

```text
wgfeel token rotate [--revision NUMBER]
```

Revoke the old administrator token and print the new token once. In the CLI this uses installed local administration only, without --profile, --socket or --credential-file (HTTP integrations can rotate tokens via POST /api/v1/token/rotate). Store the new token securely.

| Argument / option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--revision NUMBER` | Expected positive configuration revision; otherwise use the current revision. |

Example:

```sh
wgfeel token rotate
```

<a id="wgfeel-egress"></a>

### wgfeel egress


<a id="wgfeel-egress-add"></a>

### wgfeel egress add

```text
wgfeel egress add [FILE] [OPTIONS]
```

Import one provider profile. With a node and users, placement and all initial user assignments are saved together. In scripts, omitted names default to the endpoint host, omitted nodes leave the profile unassigned and omitted users grant no routes.

Accepts the [connection options](#connection-options).

| Argument / option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--config-file PATH` | Read one WireGuard provider profile from this file (16 KiB maximum). |
| `--config-stdin` | Read the provider profile from standard input through EOF. This disables all prompts. |
| `--name NAME` | Display name of the egress profile, up to 128 bytes. |
| `--node NODE_ID` | Place the profile on this eligible entry node. |
| `--users IDS` | Comma-separated user IDs. Requires a node and either --routes or --internet. |
| `--internet` | Grant the default route for each address family supported by the profile and its provider AllowedIPs. |
| `--routes CIDRS` | Comma-separated explicit route prefixes for this assignment. |
| `--dns-default` | Use eligible provider DNS servers as the user's default DNS. |
| `--dns-zones ZONES` | Use provider DNS for these comma-separated domain suffixes. |
| `--non-interactive` | Read the supplied arguments without prompting. |

Example:

```sh
wgfeel egress add office.conf
wgfeel egress add --config-stdin < office.conf
```

<a id="wgfeel-egress-node"></a>

### wgfeel egress node

```text
wgfeel egress node [EGRESS_ID] [--node NODE_ID | --unassign]
```

Inspect placement or request a global attach, move or detach. A move can remain pending until the former node releases the profile.

Accepts the [connection options](#connection-options).

| Argument / option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--node NODE_ID` | Place the profile on this eligible entry node. |
| `--unassign` | Detach the profile or cancel a pending destination. Requires confirmation at a terminal, defaulting to no. For unattended changes use the node placement REST endpoint with If-Match. |

Example:

```sh
wgfeel egress node eg_office --node entry_b
```

### wgfeel egress delete

```text

```

Accepts the [connection options](#connection-options).

Example:

```sh
wgfeel egress delete eg_office
```

<a id="wgfeel-user-egress-set"></a>

### wgfeel user egress set

```text
wgfeel user egress set [USER_ID] [EGRESS_ID] [OPTIONS]
```

Create or replace one assignment. Supply route intent; DNS defaults to none. An unassigned profile can be attached first using --node. Re-export device profiles after changing the assignment.

Accepts the [connection options](#connection-options).

| Argument / option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--node NODE_ID` | Place the profile on this eligible entry node. |
| `--internet` | Grant the default route for each address family supported by the profile and its provider AllowedIPs. |
| `--routes CIDRS` | Comma-separated explicit route prefixes for this assignment. |
| `--dns-default` | Use eligible provider DNS servers as the user's default DNS. |
| `--dns-zones ZONES` | Use provider DNS for these comma-separated domain suffixes. |
| `--non-interactive` | Read the supplied arguments without prompting. |

Example:

```sh
wgfeel user egress set alice eg_office --routes 10.40.0.0/16
```

<a id="wgfeel-user-egress-remove"></a>

### wgfeel user egress remove

```text
wgfeel user egress remove [USER_ID] [EGRESS_ID]
```

Remove one assignment after confirmation at a terminal. Re-export the affected device profiles.

Accepts the [connection options](#connection-options).

Example:

```sh
wgfeel user egress remove alice eg_office
```
